note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection. Every Tuesday she goes with her grandmother to the town clinic and has to miss school that day, and her mother cooks in two homes until evening.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: Class 6 English — Writing a Short Description of a Place

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: The teacher asks the whole class to name their favourite spot outdoors and writes the ideas on the board. The pupils call out places like a park or a playground. The materials needed are just the chalkboard and chalk.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher explains how to use sensory words like sights and sounds to describe a place clearly. The pupils listen and give examples of words that describe a busy market. The materials needed are a large chart paper and markers.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: The teacher guides the class to write a short paragraph about a familiar place using the new words. The pupils write their paragraphs individually in their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher invites volunteers to read their descriptions aloud and asks the class what they liked about each one. The pupils listen and share kind feedback. No special materials are needed.

items.heading: Homework
items.text: The teacher assigns the task of writing a five-sentence description of the school library to be done at home. The pupils note down the task in their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.
